subject: Shiny server incredibly slow on IE9

messages.author: eb140afdb010deb1
messages.subject: Shiny server incredibly slow on IE9
parts:
Sorry to have two questions in one day, I'm trying all kinds of things and throwing up more and more problems.

So have the problem with the latest version of Shiny Server as I described in my other question, I rolled back to 1.4. This is fine now, all the applications work as normal within the corporate environment on Google Chrome.

I'm trying to access applications I host on a normal (i.e. non proxied) Ubuntu 14.04 server hosted in the cloud with Shiny Server v 1.4. As I say above, they work fine on Google Chrome. However, in IE9, which I really need to support (because of the corporate environment), they run incredibly slowly. Responses that take perhaps 5 seconds on Google Chrome can take a minute or more on IE9. There are no error messages of any kind within the console of IE9.

Here's an example of one of the applications that I'm trying to get working on IE9: http://109.74.194.173:8080/apps/patientVoices/

I'm totally baffled by this behaviour, which even exists (i.e. it's very slow) on the startup application hosted at the root of the shiny apps directory http://109.74.194.173:8080/

Any ideas?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server incredibly slow on IE9
parts: SockJS (the library we use for websocket emulation) has a variety of transports. It's possible the one it's choosing is not interacting well with your corporate firewall/proxy (for example, buffering responses from the server for 60 seconds). Try pressing Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A in IE9 when an app is loaded. Try unchecking the protocols one by one (hitting reload each time). In particular, unchecking the ones named *-streaming may do the trick.

messages.author: eb140afdb010deb1
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server incredibly slow on IE9
parts:
Joe, you are, as ever, a genius. That fixed it.

Just in case it helps anyone else, it was xdr-polling that was the culprit, which means you need to add the following line to your shiny-server.conf:

disable_protocols xdr-polling;

Hey presto.

Thanks!
